Cleveland-Cliffs: 80x More on Buybacks Than Its EPA Fine

Cleveland-Cliffs spent 80x more buying back its own stock than on its EPA penalty.

2022: $240 million in stock buybacks (10-K). Same year: a $3 million EPA penalty to settle alleged Clean Water Act violations over an August 2019 wastewater discharge at Burns Harbor. 80 to 1 (our math).

Sources: Cleveland-Cliffs 10-K 2022; EPA consent decree, Feb 14, 2022.

descripcion:
Cleveland-Cliffs spent 80 times more buying back its own stock than on its EPA penalty, in the same year.

In its Form 10-K for 2022, Cleveland-Cliffs says it returned $240 million in capital to shareholders through its share repurchase program. A share repurchase, or buyback, is when a company buys back its own stock.

In February 2022, the EPA announced a consent decree (a court-approved settlement): Cleveland-Cliffs Burns Harbor agreed to pay a $3 million penalty to resolve alleged Clean Water Act violations over an August 2019 wastewater discharge from the Burns Harbor steel mill into a river.

$240 million divided by $3 million is 80 (our math). The discharge was in 2019; the penalty and the buybacks both land in 2022. Alleged violations, settled. 80 to 1.

Sources: Cleveland-Cliffs Form 10-K for 2022; EPA enforcement page and consent decree, Feb 14, 2022.
